new_statements.quote: Estos son los únicos signos modales. Para la acentuación pinto el acento allí donde lo he oído de viva voz, pues por regla general puede asentarse que el acento carga sobre la última sílaba.
new_statements.translation: These are the only modal signs. For accentuation I write the accent where I have heard it spoken aloud, since as a general rule it can be stated that the accent falls on the last syllable.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Verification done from the copies we hold under (1) Quote: I re-rendered PDF pages 309-317 of 526 pp., no text layer) into the and read the page images. PDF page 309 is the title page 'Gramática y vocabulario de la lengua que hablan los indios Darienes.. obra escrita por el señor doctor don José Vicente Uribe.. copiada de los manuscritos originales, y bajo la inspección del autor, por J. M. Quijano Otero' (printed p. 297); PDF page 311 is printed p. 299, 'Indicaciones generales / Signos', and the sentence 'Estos son los únicos signos modales. Para la acentuación pinto el acento allí donde lo he oído de viva voz, pues por regla general puede asentarse que el acento carga sobre la última síla…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the final syllable as a general rule; the author marks the accent orthographically only where he heard it, which implies the rule has exceptions. The 1876 German version of the same manuscript (ZfE 8: 359) gives only 'Accentuation ist der Accent dahin gesetzt, wo ich das Wort habe betonen hören' (the accent is placed where I heard the word stressed) with no rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Implied but not listed: the author writes the accent 'where I have heard it', and marked forms in the text include non-final accents (e.g. 'Uárra' boy, 'táma' snake, 'táira' you-pl.), so the 'general rule' is not exceptionless.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms elicited from speakers; 19th-century impressionistic notation by a non-linguist (physician), with no phonetic definition of 'acento'. Low authority; to be superseded by Mortensen 1999 or Loewen 1963 when opened.
new_statements.identity_note: The only opened statement is a 19th-century sketch by the physician José Vicente Uribe (Spanish edition copied and read by J. M. Quijano Otero, 1882; German version 1876). It describes 'embera bede' as spoken across the whole Chocó 'between the mouths of the Atrato and the San Juan and the cordillera bordering Chocó and Antioquia'; the 1876 German version names the Chamí, Andágueda, Murindó, Cañasgordas, Rioverde, Necodá, Caramanta, Tadocito, Pató and Curasamba groups, i.e. Antioquia/upper-Atrato Emberá (Emberá-Chamí [cmi] / Emberá-Catío [cto] = embe1260 territory) as much as Atrato/Darién Emberá. Glottolog files both editions under nort2972 and the 'Darienes' label is the editor's, but the sketch is pan-Emberá rather than tied to modern Northern Emberá [emp] proper. The modern reference grammar (Mortensen 1999) covers Catío [cto] and Northern Emberá [emp] together; Loewen 1958/1963 describe the Sambú (Panama) dialect = emp.
